cards.text: The flood is over, and God has set His rainbow in the clouds as a sign (Genesis 9:13). Now meet the sons of Noah who came out of the ark: Shem, Ham and Japheth. And Ham was the father of Canaan.

cards.question: Shem, Ham and Japheth are Noah's three sons. From them, the whole ___ was populated.

cards.text: Now Noah, a man of the soil, gets to planting. This man is over 600 years old (Genesis 8:13), friend, and I still groan every time I step off my gold base.

cards.question: Noah the man of the soil gets to planting. What does he plant?

cards.text: Noah drinks some of its wine, becomes drunk and uncovers himself inside his tent. Oh, friend, this family just made it through a flood, and here comes trouble.

cards.question: Ham, the father of Canaan, sees his father's nakedness inside the tent. What does Ham do?

answers.text: He tells his two brothers outside
He covers his father with a cloak
He goes in and wakes his father

cards.text: Shem and Japheth take a garment and lay it across their shoulders. They're going to cover their dad, and they've got a plan.

cards.question: Shem and Japheth have the garment across their shoulders. How do they get to their father?
Shem and Japheth see their father's nakedness while they cover him.

cards.text: Walking BACKWARD. Carrying a garment. Faces turned the other way. These two would rather trip over a tent peg than see their dad like that.
When Noah wakes up, he learns what his youngest son had done to him. And notice this: twice now, the text has called Ham the father of Canaan.

cards.question: Noah has learned what his youngest son did to him, and he speaks a curse. Who does Noah curse?
In his curse, Noah says Canaan will be a ___ to his brothers.

cards.text: Then Noah declares, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem!" Look close, friend: the one being blessed in that line is the LORD Himself.

cards.question: Right after blessing the LORD, the God of Shem, Noah says may Canaan be Shem's servant.
Noah has words for Japheth too. He asks God to expand Japheth's ___.

cards.text: Then Noah adds, "may he dwell in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant." Three brothers, and all their futures in one speech.
The flood came when Noah was 600 years old (Genesis 7:6), and after it he lives another 350 years. Three hundred fifty MORE, friend, and I can't even wait out a ten-minute oven timer.

cards.question: Noah was 600 when the flood came, and he lived 350 years after it. How many years does Noah live in all?

cards.text: Now comes the account of Noah's sons Shem, Ham and Japheth, who also had sons after the flood. Japheth's line goes first: Gomer, Magog, Javan and more. From these, the maritime peoples separated into their territories, by language and clan.
Next up is Ham's line: Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan. And Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth.

cards.question: Nimrod, son of Cush, began to be a mighty one on the earth. What is Nimrod known as?

cards.text: He's so known for it that it becomes a saying: "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD." Friend, nobody has EVER said "Like Dorin, a mighty stamper." Not out loud, anyway.

cards.question: Nimrod the mighty hunter has a kingdom. Where does his kingdom begin?
Once his kingdom begins in the land of Shinar, Nimrod stays there for good.
Nimrod goes from Shinar into Assyria, and there he builds the city of ___.

cards.text: The rest of Ham's line fills in fast. It includes the Philistines, the Hittites, the Jebusites and the Amorites, and Canaan's borders reach from Sidon as far as Gaza and toward Sodom and Gomorrah.

Last comes Shem, the older brother of Japheth. In his line, Eber has a son named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and Peleg's brother Joktan has THIRTEEN sons. I had six little cutters on one counter and thought THAT was a crowd.

cards.question: From the clans of Noah's sons, the ___ of the earth spread out after the flood.

findings.problem: This story card only retells Genesis 9:23, which cards 7, 8 and 9 already covered: the garment, walking backward and faces turned away. It recaps instead of moving the passage forward.

The question says Noah "asks God to expand Japheth's ___." Genesis 9:27 is a pronouncement ("May God expand the territory of Japheth"), not a request made to God. This is the same case as the Naomi example.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The storyteller line "Three brothers, and all their futures in one speech" adds a fact the text doesn't support. Noah's words in Genesis 9:25-27 speak about Canaan, Shem and Japheth. They say nothing about Ham's own future.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action. Noah lives 350 more years, but the comparison is about impatiently waiting out an oven timer. Living a long time and waiting for something are different actions.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 18 gives both numbers (600 at the flood, 350 more after), and the question repeats them. The answer is just 600 + 350, which rules out 969 and 930 without the baker reading Genesis 9:29.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question calls Nimrod "a mighty one," and only the right answer repeats that word ("A mighty hunter"). The other answers are "A famous musician" and "A wise counselor," so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card cites Genesis 10:21-31, but the last verse it uses is 10:29, where Joktan's thirteen sons end. Verses 10:30-31 (Joktan's territory and the closing line for Shem) aren't told, so the citation is too wide.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "rivers" and "forests" aren't the same kind of thing as "nations." Clans can't produce rivers or forests, so the wrong answers aren't believable and the right answer is obvious.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Genesis 10 is a genealogy with a short narrative about Nimrod (10:8-12) in the middle of it. The stop sums up the genealogy in four story cards (cards 1, 2, 8 and 9) instead of one. It also gives choice cards to the Nimrod verses (cards 3, 5, 6 and 7) and to the genealogy's closing verse, 10:32 (card 10).
findings.question: When a long stretch like a genealogy has a short narrative inside it, is the narrative part of the stretch or its own moment that can get choice cards? Can the stretch be summed up in several story cards, such as one per son's line? And can the stretch's closing summary verse (10:32) get a choice card?
